title: Epochal frontier admission prober for soft-horizon continuous batching
author: Aisha Cheng
description: Summary: Implements an 'Epochal Frontier Admission Prober' (EAP) for the continuous batching scheduler to reduce starvation for KV-heavy and short-lived requests while preserving throughput for long sequences. Motivation: we've observed recurring tail latency regressions under mixed workloads when aggressive prefix caching and long batching windows are enabled. Existing fixes (shorter windows, conservative admission limits) either hurt throughput or increase cost. EAP introduces a lightweight, epoch-based admission probe that temporarily lowers admission thresholds for requests at the queue frontier, with jittered short leases and a soft-horizon window to prevent repeated preemption. The design is conservative: probes are sampled per-epoch and back off exponentially on contention.

discussion_resolution: Added tenant-scoped metrics and debug tracing
Reduced backoff aggressiveness and expanded soft-horizon window
Fixed atomic race in prober state transitions
Benchmarks added and documented in docs/benchmarks/epochal_admission.md
performance_summary: Testbed: 8xA10 nodes, mixed workload: 60% short-KV (<=128 tokens), 40% long gen (>=1024 tokens)
P50 throughput: baseline 9.3k tokens/s -> with EAP 9.1k tokens/s (-1.8%)
Cost impact: negligible token cost change; better SLA compliance reduces tail-driven retries
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature flag default=off; enable for internal canary (redwood-dedicated-canary namespace) for 48h
Stage 2: enable for 10% of production requests (routing config) with tenant-metrics exported to Grafana for 72h
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring alerts for probe_grant_rate and p99 latency regressions
Rollback: feature flag off; prober is idempotent and drains immediately (no stateful migration required)
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: if grants_total/denials_total ratio > 0.8 and p99_short_kv_latency increases by >10% for 10m => auto rollback candidate
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: over-admission could increase tail for long sequences. Mitigation: prober samples primarily at the queue frontier and uses soft-horizon to prevent repeated grants to same tenant.
Risk: increased scheduler complexity. Mitigation: prober is feature-flagged and opt-in; code paths are small and well-covered by unit/integration tests.
Risk: metric explosion for high-tenant cardinality. Mitigation: tenant-scoped metrics are cardinality-limited and aggregated for dashboards by default.
release_notes: Introduce epochal frontier admission prober for continuous batching to reduce tail latency for KV-heavy short requests. Configurable via scheduler.prober.* knobs. (non-breaking, opt-in behind flag)
Add new scheduler metrics and debug tracing to support rollout and incident analysis.
